name: Finland

income_tax.summary: State progressive scale (12.64% to 37.5% as PwC lists it) plus municipal tax of 4.70-10.90% (7.5% used). Employee contributions about 10.17%; YEL for self-employed 24.4%.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: YEL pension 24.4% of confirmed income in 2026 (Ilmarinen), with a 22% discount on the contribution for new entrepreneurs (YEL insurance in force under four years); minimum confirmed income EUR 9,423.09. Self-employed also pay Kela health contributions, which were not found on a page opened. Employee (PwC 2026): pension 7.30% + unemployment 0.89% + health 1.98% (1.10% medicare + 0.88% daily allowance, the latter not collected below EUR 17,255 of salary).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Municipal tax ranges 4.70-10.90% on PwC (Wikipedia gives a 2025 average of 9.28% and a 4.7-19.7% range, which conflicts); PwC's 7.5% is described as the average for non-residents and is used as a stand-in because Helsinki's own rate was not confirmed on any page opened. Church tax (1-2.25%) excluded. The brackets add PwC's state-scale rates to 7.5% and apply from the first euro; Finnish earned-income deductions are not modelled.

PwC's table (12.64% / 19% / 30.25% / 33.25% / 37.5%, first limit shown as both 21,200 and 22,000) and Wikipedia's 2025 table (12.64 / 19 / 30.25 / 34 / 41.75 / 44.25 with limits at 88,200 and 150,000) disagree above EUR 52,100, which matters at EUR 130,000. regimes.name: Key employee regime (avainhenkilö)
regimes.description: Foreign key employees with special knowledge can be taxed at a flat 25% on Finnish-source salary from the primary employment (PwC 2026; the rate was 32% before 2026). Minimum cash salary of EUR 5,800 in every month, not Finnish resident in the previous five calendar years, up to 84 months; apply within 90 days of starting work. Local employment required. Final tax: no deductions against that income.
regimes.duration_note: Up to 84 months for foreign nationals (60 for returning Finns).

open_questions: Only PwC opened; vero.fi's key-employee pages returned 404/no content. Whether municipal tax is included in the 25% and whether social contributions are due on top was not verified (they normally are).

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Average 2026 rent for a Helsinki 1-bedroom (about 38-48 m2), derived from Statistics Finland rent data (StatFin 15fa, Q1 2026) with assumed unit size; range EUR 900-1,600.

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Average 2026 rent for a Helsinki 2-bedroom (about 58-70 m2), same derivation; range EUR 1,250-2,400.

costs.notes: Modelled estimate from Investropa (Statistics Finland as base, assumed unit sizes of 38-48 and 58-70 m2); no listing sample and no per-room-type table values. Page states a citywide private-market average of about EUR 24 per m2.

residence_routes: EU/EEA citizens register their right of residence. Third-country nationals (US included) need a residence permit for an employed person, or a specialist permit; Finland has no digital nomad visa identified in this research (not verified on Migri).
open_questions: State tax scale and Helsinki municipal rate unconfirmed.
Nomad visa absence and non-EU permits not verified on Migri.
